newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden may cut repo rate again next week - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Sweden may cut repo rate again next week - analysts.

text.p: With inflation down and out, at least for the moment, Sweden's central bank could be tempted to cut its key repurchase rate still further next week.

A lower repo rate could be announced as early as Tuesday, November 26, when the present series of four reverse repos at a fixed 4.60 percent runs out, according to economists and money market analysts polled by Reuters.

"We believe there will be a cut of 20-25 basis points. There is an even chance of a cut on Tuesday but they could also decide to wait a bit," said Sven-Arne Svensson, economist at Hagstromer & Qviberg.
The most powerful argument for a cut in the repo rate, the Riksbank's main tool for controlling money market liquidity, is consumer price inflation.
In October the CPI index was unchanged from September to give a minus 0.1 percent year-on-year rate, the first time for 37 years it had fallen into deflation.
Many believe that inflation will stay below zero when the figures for November are published on December 12.
"Our preliminary calculations are that it will fall still further to 0.2 percent," says Peter Lindqvist, economist at HSBC Midland.
Lindqvist is expecting a repo cut by at least 15 basis points, either next week or perhaps after the Riksbank publishes its next inflation report on December 17.
"Then they would have household purchasing for November and Prosperas inflation survey as background," Lindqvist said.
Beshara Mahdi, economist at Morgan Stanley, thinks the Riksbank would be unwise to hold its fire until December 17.
"I can see nothing that argues against a cut next week. Waiting almost a month could be harmful for the money market," he said.
Morgan Stanley is one of the more bullish on interest rates, reckoning on a base of 3.75 percent next spring for the repo rate, which is the central rate in a three tier system.
The Riksbank last lowered the repo rate by 25 basis points on October 24. This was the 23rd cut this year with the repo rate starting 1996 at 8.91 percent.
At the same time the bank cut deposit and loan rates by 50 basis points, to 4.25 percent and 5.75 percent respectively.
Economists said data released since that date argued in favour of a repo cut.
Sven-Arne Svensson noted that the Riksbank had set an inflation target of one to three percent for 1996.
"It looks as if the average for 1996 is going to land around 0.8 percent and so the inflation target will be missed," Svensson said.
